# Flow audit — after_233fcc9c

*Generated by `tools/flow-audit.mjs` from `out/flow-audit/after-233fcc9c/samples.jsonl` (sampler: `tools/harness/flow-sampler.mjs`). Build 233fcc9c. The rule is UIB_JOB_16: need = 2 s + 0.4 s per word (cap 10 s); a press ends text legitimately; nothing opens on top of what is being read; one voice at a time.*

## How to read this

- **too fast** — a text block that left the screen by itself (no press in the second before) before its need. Lines that arrived together are one block and read together. A text that grew longer (typing) or re-wrapped or is still elsewhere on the same canvas has not left.
- **overlap** — *hidden* / *partly covered*: a text run under a LATER opaque draw in the same canvas frame (a window, card, banner, picture or child canvas blitted over it) that started by itself; *text on text*: two visible texts printing over each other.
- **voices** — three or more distinct places (canvas + a 3×3 cell of it) getting new text within ~4 s, or a guide balloon up while something else is new. Only arrivals no press asked for.
- **stream** — three or more lines arriving unprompted less than 1.5 s apart (the job's "at least 1.5 s per line" for changelogs).
- **guide** — the guide hook (`__guide()` side message, or Lamby's balloon) said a line was active but its text was never drawn on any canvas while it was active. In 1997 the side message is drawn only while the pointer rests on the helper tip (src/desktop/os.ts `guideTipAt`), so an unprompted side message is invisible; Lamby's balloon is the visible one.
- **clock** — a clock text that jumps 20 min or more inside two minutes (rule 4).
- **flicker** — a text that was on screen for 0.6 s or less and left by itself (a blink, a glitch frame): listed so a blinking prompt is not invisible.
- Times are seconds from the start of the sampled walk, **wall-clock**. A "canvas" is an offscreen 2D surface; rects are in that canvas's own pixels (the OS desktop is 512×384, Room 2's workstation 676×390 plus a draw scale, the handset 180×360 at 2×).
- **Not in a failure count:** the by-design EXCEPTIONS (their own table, with the reason), and anything a walker press ended. The tool sees canvas text only, not DOM captions or the pixel games' rect letters, and it cannot know which surface the player is facing.

## The run

- 10122 samples over 42:10 (2530 s), 736 walker presses, 776 walker log lines, 19 canvases seen.
- Frame rate while sampled: median 60 fps, 0.0 % of samples under 12 fps (the piece's clock and the wall clock agree).
- Eras as the walker tracked them (`os.desktopEra`): **1997** 0:01–8:15, **2003** 8:15–17:01, **2016** 17:01–23:03, **2026** 23:03–42:10
- 6618 text lines were seen arriving and 5200 blocks; 4000 lines left earlier than their need, of which a press ended 2291 (not counted); 429 covered/overprinted texts began right after a press (not counted).

## Exceptions in force

Named in `tools/flow-audit.mjs` `EXCEPTIONS`; a hit is reported above, never counted as a failure.

- **2016-cascade** (7 hits) — The 2016 cascade's speed is the point ("outnumbered", s3_maiden.json `cascade`, graceQueueLite CASCADE_STEP): the group's forwards land faster than review can answer, and the piece says so. Only the PHONE's group thread while stage is `takeover` is exempt — the board's PRIORITY ALERT cards, the Review rows and Orla's message are not.
- **2026-clip** (6 hits) — The 2026 clip ("The Great Becoming", Second Thoughts' AI-made video) is timed to its music and narrator, and its cards are the beat (S360/S364, Sérgio 11 Nov: "the sound is fantastic, love the check marks and the intensity of each of the signs"). Its cards stay exactly as timed. Matched by the browser's clip takeover being live, or by the clip's own strings (data/dialog/s4_v3.json `clip`).
- **1997-update-cascade** (4 hits) — The 1997 update arrives as a CASCADE of error windows that pile on one another and on the desk ("the beat is that there is nothing to fight", src/desktop/apps/update.ts `cascade`; SCRIPT_UPDATE v0.5). Windows covering windows is the picture. Only while the u2 ritual is in its `cascade` phase.
- **desktop-icons** (4 hits) — A desktop icon's label under an open window is how a desktop works (1997 / 2003: "Session", "rootcause.", "Family Form", "Care Log"); an icon is not a reading surface, and the window over it is the one in use.
- **2003-redaction** (28 hits) — Restorify blacks out Caleb's thread line by line, and later gives it back line by line (src/desktop/apps/caleb.ts, the redaction walk). The words were on screen and read before it began; the line-by-line removal and return is the system's act on them, and the transcript follows the walk.
- **2026-ai-acting** (2 hits) — His brief (UIB_JOB_16 Part B): "The banner itself may be brief: it is the AI acting." The green "Second Thoughts is using your computer" bar comes and goes with the AI's act on her computer (browser.ts `act`). Only the bar itself, nothing the AI says in the chat.
- **2026-ball** (17 hits) — The ball is deliberate stillness, about 3½ minutes with no controls, its lines timed to the audio (memory: stillness-is-not-a-dead-end; src/desktop/apps/ball.ts). Anything drawn while the ball is live is timed by the recording, not by a reader.

## Not checked

- DOM text (captions, the frame's menu, the entrance's own panels): only canvas text is drawn here.
- Which surface the player is facing: a surface behind the head that redraws still counts.
- Sound: whether a voice or a clip overlaps another is invisible here (headless, no audio).
- The walker's press rhythm (about 2.2 s) hides every "too fast" a press ended; the report counts those in the run summary only.
